newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks hit new record, despite Roche slide.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks hit new record, despite Roche slide.

text.p: A late slide in the certificates of Swiss pharmaceuticals group Roche Holding AG wiped out most of the market's early gains, but the share indices still ended at a new record close.
The decline in Roche was triggered by Roche's statement's that the acquisition of Boehringer Mannheim Group for around $11 billion would cause a significant dilution of earnings in the first year.
"After this, the stock came down rapidly," one trader noted.
Sentiment, however, remained optimistic, a dealer added.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended 15.7 points, or 0.3 percent, higher at 5,196.7 points. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 11.83 points, or 0.36 percent, to 3,284.68.
Bourse volume was at 2.66 billion francs. Activity was also heavily influenced by derivative transactions.
One dealer said some profit taking could pressure prices in the next few sessions, but the outlook remained favourable.
"The targets that most brokers have set for the SMI may have already been met and I think and they will by adjusted soon," one trader noted.
Roche ended down 185 francs, or 1.4 percent, at 13,005 after earlier hitting an all-time high of 13,745.
One dealer said a jump in Ciba SC Chemicals, which powered ahead 8.75 francs to 151.75, was probably due to derivatives-related transactions.
Among financial shares, CS Group was up four francs to 187.
Industrial Sulzer added 51 francs to 1,190 after the company said it received a Russion order for two multi-phase pumps which it described as a "break-through" expected to lead to more orders.
Nestle, SBC and Surveillance were lower among blue-chips and second-tier Oerlikon-Buehrle slid 7.50 frans to 156.
